label: vanilla-1836-rebase
_why: REBASE THE 1836 SCENARIOS ON A FRESH SAVE OF THE CURRENT GAME (user, 2026-08-13). config/measured_1836.json was extracted on 2026-08-03 against an older build; the game is now 1.13.10, whose hotfix notes touch quantities the scenarios are calibrated against. The 1836 real-country scenarios are meant to be FAITHFUL to vanilla whatever we think of the concepts inside them, so their inputs have to be re-read from the game rather than carried forward. This run supplies both halves at one tick: the TELEMETRY that history files cannot answer (trade, SoL by stratum, military levels, urban-centre PMs, wages) and, via monthly autosaves, a SAVEGAME at 1836.2.1 for the state-side readers.
_arms: {kind: control} — vanilla + telemetry and nothing else. This measures THE GAME, so it must not carry our content; a modded arm here would rebase the scenarios on ourselves.
_comparison: Against config/measured_1836.json as it stands (extracted 2026-08-03) and against what extract_presets.ps1 derives from the history files. Differences get reported, not silently applied — the history files are the AUTHORED start and the save is the INITIALISED one, and which should win differs per field.
_watch: 1836.2.1 and NOT day 0: construction goods spend is exactly £0 on 1836.1.1 because the sector has not ticked (FINDINGS F14), so day 0 is history-faithful and economically unfinished. Whether the savegame diverges much from the history-derived state is itself the question — urban-centre levels and the pop-class split are the two most likely to move.
_cost: 3 runs x 2 in-game months, ~3 minutes. extract_measured averages field by field, which is its documented default because the 1836 start is nearly deterministic for most metrics but NOT all (urban-centre tram levels swing by a third between runs, F16).
_caveats: GAME 1.13.10. Metric set matches the belgium_check/allmarkets_popsol lineage that produced the current measured_1836.json, so the two are comparable field by field. Tags are the eight preset countries, which is what config/presets.json drives. ⚠ n=3 because the FIRST single-run attempt showed military type counts and trade breadth well below the committed reference, which is exactly the shape single-run coverage noise takes; averaging is how extract_measured is meant to be fed.
